---
pagetitle: "psychometrician"
listing:
  contents: posts
  sort: "date desc"
  type: default
  categories: true
  fields: [image, date, title, reading-time, description, categories]
  # Nothing changes until there are more than ten posts, and then numbered pages
  # appear instead of a front page that scrolls for five thousand pixels. Set
  # now rather than later, because the default is to show every post forever and
  # it degrades quietly: no warning, just a page that keeps getting longer.
  page-size: 10
  feed:
    # `full` is already the default in Quarto 1.8, and it is written out anyway.
    # An unrecognized value here does not fail: it falls through to a feed of
    # metadata only, which looks like a feed and carries no article. R-bloggers
    # and JuliaBloggers both want the whole text.
    type: full
    items: 10
    language: en-us
    # One extra feed per name, written to `index-<name>.xml` beside the main
    # one. The match against a post's own `categories:` is exact and case
    # sensitive, and only the filename is lowered, never slugified, so a name
    # with a space in it produces a filename with a space in it. Single words.
    #
    # Two names and not four, because only two of the four communities pull.
    # R-bloggers and JuliaBloggers each take a feed address once and republish
    # from it forever. Python and JavaScript have no equivalent: PyCoder's
    # Weekly wants a form filled in per post and JavaScript Weekly wants an
    # email, so a `python.xml` would have no subscriber.
    #
    # These two are worth writing even while every post carries every language
    # and all three feeds come out identical. The address given to an aggregator
    # is given once and is awkward to change, so the question is not which feed
    # is right today but which is still right after the first post that is not
    # about all four. `index.xml` would carry that one to R-bloggers; this does
    # not. A category here means the post belongs in that community's feed, not
    # that the language is mentioned in it.
    categories: [rstats, julialang]
page-layout: full
# The card for this page, named here even though `_quarto.yml` sets the same
# file as the site default. Without it Quarto prefers the first image on the
# page over that default, and the first image here is the hex sticker, which is
# portrait. Bluesky letterboxes a portrait card and X drops to a small square
# thumbnail instead of a banner. So the front page, the one address most people
# paste, was the one page whose card came out wrong.
image: images/og.png
image-alt: >-
  gog, a grammar of graphics. One engine, spoken from R, Python, Julia and
  JavaScript.
---

::: {.site-hero-text}
# We build packages for data manipulation and visualization.

**god** is a grammar of data: one vocabulary for tables, spoken from R, Python
and SQL. The same pipeline runs on your laptop and on a cluster.

[Say it once. Run it anywhere.]{.site-slogan .site-slogan-god}

**gog** is a grammar of graphics: one engine written in Rust, spoken from R,
Python, Julia and JavaScript. Describe a plot in any of the four and you get the
same picture, not a similar one.

[Be agog. Use gog.]{.site-slogan}

The posts below are short pieces, each introducing one part of one package. Both
have a book: [god's](https://psychometrician.github.io/god-book/) and
[gog's](https://psychometrician.github.io/gog-book/), which has 654 plots and not
one screenshot among them.
:::
:::
